attempts.label: DANDI:000061
attempts.paper_title: Reactivations of emotional memory in the hippocampus–amygdala system during sleep
attempts.entry_title: Hippocampus and amygdala reactivation during sleep (Girardeau et al. 2017)
attempts.description: Tests the claims of Girardeau, Inema and Buzsaki (2017), written from the full text, the supplement and the paper's code, on dandiset 000061, which holds sorted units of the hippocampus and the amygdala, sleep states, ripple, air puff and reward events from four rats on an air puff linear track task. It tests the unit counts, habituation over days, BLA firing by sleep state, hippocampus-BLA and hippocampus-central nuclei reactivation (explained variance) with all cells, and the ripple rate before and after training. Claims on putative pyramidal cells and on position are blocked, as the dandiset holds neither.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Girardeau et al. (2017) from dandiset 000061

outcomes.statement: Over 61 sessions in 4 rats, 7,390 well-isolated units were recorded (rat 1, 2,444; rat 2, 1,294; rat 3, 1,138; rat 4, 2,514), of which 2,038 were in the BLA, 782 in the central nuclei, 1,560 in the piriform cortex and 1,210 in the hippocampus.
outcomes.source: Results, BLA recordings and sleep physiology, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 1
outcomes.quote: Over the course of a total of 61 sessions, we recorded 7,390 well-isolated units (rat 1, 2,444; rat 2, 1,294; rat ... 3, 1,138; rat 4, 2,514). On the basis of histological reconstruction of probe placement and probe movement record, 2,038 of these were in the BLA, 782 in the central nuclei, 1,560 in the piriform cortex and 1,210 in the hippocampus
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 40 sessions (33 with a units table) and 4702 units, against 61 sessions and 7,390 units, both outside the 10% tolerance, so the criterion's totals fail. Only Rat08, taken as rat 1, is within tolerance (2317 against 2,444); Rat09, Rat10 and Rat11 hold 515, 440 and 1430 against 1,294, 1,138 and 2,514. By label there are 1118 BLA (bla and BLA), 482 central nuclei, 935 piriform and 829 hippocampal units against 2,038, 782, 1,560 and 1,210; the wider amygdala labels (bla, blv, bmp, ladl) give 1977. The difference is in the data deposited, fewer days and units than the paper reports. No outcome in the earlier attempt, which had no such claim.
deviations: The dandiset does not say which of Rat08 to Rat11 are the paper's rats 1 to 4. Rat09, the rat without hippocampal units, is taken as rat 2 (whose hippocampal probe failed) and the others in order; this is an assumption.
Units are counted as stored, one per session, including units 0 and 1 of the ten files whose spike index is wrong; location counts use the dandiset's labels read as the paper's structures.

outcomes.statement: The aversive valence of the air puff diminishes over training days; rats run more laps per unit time as they habituate.
outcomes.source: Results, Rats learn the daily location of an aversive air puff on a linear track, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 1c
outcomes.quote: The aversive valence of the air puff gradually diminished with training days (Supplementary Fig. 1c).
outcomes.notes: Under O1 reading c, over 40 sessions of four rats, the habituation index rises with training day for each lap count, pooled Spearman rho 0.383 (p = 0.015) for all laps, 0.331 (p = 0.046, 37 sessions with a puff direction) for air puff laps and 0.397 (p = 0.011) for left-to-right laps. The correlation is positive in all four rats for each count, with p < 0.05 in Rat08, Rat09 and Rat10 and not in Rat11 (rho 0.32 to 0.33). Both readings of "gradually diminished" hold for all three counts, so the outcome holds under every reading the dandiset allows. The answer to this attempt's question (questions/000061.yaml) confirmed that the claim is judged on O1 reading c alone when the dataset holds neither lap intervals nor position, and the criterion now says so; the outcome, reproduced before the answer, is unchanged. No outcome in the earlier attempt.
deviations: Laps are O1 reading c, the intervals between consecutive rewards at opposite ends with both rewards inside the run. Reading a has no lap intervals in the dandiset (its trials table is not laps) and reading b needs position, which it lacks. As answered, the claim is judged on reading c alone; the hand-picked 150-cm window of ClassifyLaps.m is not reproduced by any reading. A reading c lap runs from reward to reward, so it includes the time on the starting platform and any stop, which the M8 laps leave out; the count of laps is the same either way.

The air puff direction of a day is the lap direction holding most puffs (1153 of 1197 puffs fall in run laps of that direction); the dandiset gives no direction. Rat08-20130709 has no puff inside a run lap and has no air puff count.
Training day is the rank of the recording date within each rat, over the 40 files; the paper's 55 behaviour sessions include days the dandiset does not hold.

outcomes.statement: BLA pyramidal cells fire faster in REM sleep and, to a lesser extent, in NREM sleep than in wakefulness.
outcomes.source: Results, BLA recordings and sleep physiology, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
outcomes.quote: we found a specific increase in the firing rate of BLA pyramidal cells, but not interneurons, during REM sleep and, to a lesser extent, NREM sleep relative to wakefulness

statistics.about: NREM/wake firing rate ratio of BLA pyramidal cells
REM/wake firing rate ratio of BLA pyramidal cells

outcomes.notes: On the 152 identified excitatory BLA units of five Rat08 sessions, the REM/wake ratio has a median of 0.39 (positive in 120, p = 7.0e-15) and the NREM/wake ratio a median of 0.18 (positive in 108, p = 7.2e-12); both are positive and the REM median exceeds the NREM median. By session the REM ratio reaches p < 0.05 in four of five sessions and the NREM ratio in three (Rat08-20130713, 22 cells, reaches neither). The paper had 675 cells from four rats; these 152 come from one rat, a smaller sample. The answer to this attempt's question (questions/000061.yaml) confirmed that the claim is judged on O4 reading a alone, the identified cells of the Fig. 2c legend, and O4 now says so; the outcome, reproduced before the answer, is unchanged. No outcome in the earlier attempt.
deviations: Cells are the units the dandiset's cell_type column marks excitatory, read as the paper's monosynaptically identified pyramidal cells (O4 reading a). The column exists in five Rat08 files only, so the test uses one rat and about a fifth of the paper's cells. Reading b (all putative pyramidal cells) cannot be formed; as answered, it is not needed for the outcome.
Units 0 and 1 of files with a wrong spike index are left out (Rat08-20130710 and 20130711).

outcomes.statement: BLA interneurons do not change their firing rate between REM sleep and wake, and fire slightly less in NREM sleep than in wake.
outcomes.source: Figure 2c legend
outcomes.quote: Interneurons do not change firing rates between REM and wake ... and slightly decrease firing rates during NREM compared to wake

statistics.about: REM/wake firing rate ratio of BLA interneurons
NREM/wake firing rate ratio of BLA interneurons

outcomes.notes: On the 36 identified inhibitory BLA units of five Rat08 sessions, the REM/wake ratio has a median of 0.029 (positive in 22) with two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.020, so the paper's test finds a REM change the claim says is absent. The NREM/wake ratio has a negative median (-0.035, positive in 16) with p = 0.26, so the decrease is not significant. Neither part holds, which the criterion calls not reproduced. By session only Rat08-20130711 (12 cells) has a REM ratio with p < 0.05. The paper had 175 interneurons from four rats; the REM effect here is small (median 0.029) and rests on one rat. The answer to this attempt's question (questions/000061.yaml) confirmed that the claim is judged on O4 reading a alone; the outcome, not reproduced before the answer, is unchanged. As context (decides nothing), the REM effect size r is 0.39 against the paper's 0.09 and the bootstrap 95% interval of the REM median is -0.015 to 0.109; the NREM r is -0.19 against the paper's -0.45, and with 36 cells a NREM shift of about 0.068 would be detected with 80% power. A short-latency cross-correlogram check finds an inhibitory partner at p < 1e-6 for 34 of the 36 inhibitory units (94.4%), against 2.0% of excitatory and 7.9% of unclassified BLA units, consistent with the column marking identified interneurons. No outcome in the earlier attempt.
deviations: Cells are the units marked inhibitory in the five typed Rat08 files, read as the paper's identified interneurons (O4 reading a, which as answered decides alone); reading b cannot be formed.

outcomes.notes: The criterion needs four NREM tests, two on putative pyramidal pairs, so it cannot be decided. As a description, with all pairs the hippocampus reactivates in NREM (23 sessions, EV above REV in 19, p = 0.0054) and the BLA does not reach p < 0.05 (16 sessions, 9, p = 0.14); in REM neither does (p = 0.83 and 0.21). Since the BLA all-pairs NREM test fails, the claim could at best be partially reproduced even with putative types. A BLA-only variant on the identified excitatory units (five Rat08 sessions, each with at least six) gives EV above REV in 4 of 5, p = 0.44, and five sessions cannot reach p < 0.05 (smallest two-sided p 0.0625); no file has six identified excitatory hippocampal units. No outcome in the earlier attempt.

outcomes.notes: With all cells over 14 sessions (the paper had 27), the air puff template is more reactivated around post-NREM than pre-NREM ripples in 10 (one-tailed p = 0.01), the safe template in 12 (p = 0.0043), and the air puff change exceeds the safe change in 8 (one-tailed p = 0.48), so both within-trajectory tests have p < 0.05 and the between-trajectory test has p >= 0.05. By rat the air puff template rises in 7 of 8 Rat08, 2 of 3 Rat10 and 1 of 3 Rat11 sessions, so its result rests mostly on Rat08. Reading c laps include the time on the starting platform and stops (median lap 22.6 s, but minutes long in early Rat08 sessions); leaving out Rat08-20130708, the only session with fewer than 3 laps in a template (one safe lap of 23 s), gives air puff p = 0.0052, safe p = 0.0052 and air puff greater than safe p = 0.37 (13 sessions). Long laps are not limited to that session (median air puff laps of 660 s in Rat08-20130711, 192 s in Rat08-20130710 and 46 to 115 s in four other Rat08 sessions), so two further variants, with values of the author's that decide nothing, limit the platform time and stops. With laps of at most 30 s (11 sessions) the result is the same (air puff p = 0.034, safe p = 0.021, air puff greater than safe p = 0.71). With each lap cut to its last 10 s (14 sessions) the air puff test holds (p = 0.034) but the safe test does not reach p < 0.05 (10 of 14, p = 0.052), and air puff greater than safe has p = 0.36. The result under the criterion's laps thus depends in part on the time around the run that reading c laps hold; the criterion fixes reading c, so the outcome is unchanged. Before the answers to this attempt's questions (questions/000061.yaml) the claim was blocked as metadata_insufficient through aversive-direction-stronger; the answers removed that dependency, the claim using that claim's procedure but not its result, and confirmed that laps are judged on O1 reading c alone here. No outcome in the earlier attempt.
deviations: Laps are O1 reading c (between rewards at opposite ends); the dandiset has no lap intervals or position. The air puff direction of a day is the lap direction holding most puffs. These laps include the time on the starting platform after each reward and any stop, so the air puff and safe templates hold awake activity off the track that the M8 laps (position inside a 150-cm window) leave out.
BLA is the bla label (case ignored); units 0 and 1 of the files with a wrong spike index are left out.

findings.statement: New in this attempt. The putative cell types the paper uses (pyramidal cell or interneuron for every unit, from monosynaptic connections and then k-means on the waveform) are not in the dandiset, and there are no spike waveforms. Five of the 33 files with units (Rat08-20130709 to 20130713) have a cell_type column with the values excitatory, inhibitory and unclassified, described only as "Type of cell this has been classified as."; it marks 152 excitatory and 36 inhibitory BLA units and 9 excitatory hippocampal units, consistent with the paper's monosynaptic identification alone. A short-latency cross-correlogram check supports this reading of the column. At p < 1e-6, 99.3% of the excitatory BLA units excite and 94.4% of the inhibitory ones inhibit another loaded unit at 1 to 4 ms, against 44% and 7.9% of the unclassified ones. Most of the paper's reactivation analyses cannot be repeated (17 claims blocked for this alone). The earlier attempt did not read this column.

New in this attempt. The dandiset holds 40 recording days with 4702 units, where the paper reports 61 sessions with 7,390 units; per rat it holds 2317, 515, 440 and 1430 units (Rat08 to Rat11) against 2,444, 1,294, 1,138 and 2,514. Which rat is which of the paper's rats 1 to 4 is not stated.

New in this attempt. The archive's asset metadata (variableMeasured) is wrong for all 40 files on two entries. It lists ElectricalSeries for the 24 files that hold no raw voltage and not for the 16 that hold it (acquisition/ElectricalSeries in Rat08-20130708 to 20130713 and all Rat09 files), and ProcessingModule for the 16 files without a behavior module and not for the 24 with one. Its Units entries agree with the files.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01; the version and the files are unchanged, and the draft holds the same assets). The epochs table is stored in milliseconds although its columns say seconds; in all 40 files its last stop time is exactly 1000 times the LFP duration.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). Video timestamps are stated in seconds but are in milliseconds and are not on the session clock; the first timestamp matches the start of the video's epoch in 1 of 114 videos, while the spans match the epoch durations in 93 of 114.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). In ten files the spike_times_index is wrong at the first units; unit 1's spike times fall back once, after 65536 times k spikes, and unit 0 stops where unit 1 starts, so the first part of unit 1 is the end of unit 0. Units 0 and 1 of these files were left out of the analyses.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). Seven files have no units table, sixteen have no sleep states and fourteen have no ripple events; the Rat09 files have no hippocampal units and no ripples.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). There is no position tracking and no air puff location, only the puff times and the raw video frames, so behaviour on the track cannot be measured without tracking about 1.9 million frames; laps and the air puff direction can only be inferred from reward and puff times.

Still present in the dandiset (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). Unit region labels are undescribed short codes (bla, blv, bmp, ladl, cen, den, ven, pir, plc01, PLCo1, cpu, hpc, HIP, no label), some in two cases, Rat09-20140328 has no location column, and the electrode table gives every channel as unknown. The paper's Supplementary Fig. 3 names the structures the codes match (BLA, BLV, LaDL, BMA, BMP, Pir, VEn, DEn), which lets this attempt read them; the dandiset still does not describe them.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). The trials table of the Rat08 and Rat09 files is described only as "experimental trials"; its intervals of 3 to 5 s fall partly outside the run and are not laps.

Still present (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01). The ripple annotations carry an undescribed number in each label (for example "Ripple peak 156"), one per file, presumably the detection channel; ripples, puffs and rewards are stored as annotation series under stimulus presentation.

Partly fixed (found by 000061-girardeau-2017-01, when the paper's text was not available). The full text was supplied for this attempt and the paper links its code (github.com/buzsakilab/papers, GGirardeau-BLAHpcInteractions-Package), which the claims file's reader read; the dandiset itself still links no analysis code, its related resources naming only the paper.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive's asset metadata and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs (EV and REV, pair correlations, the Poisson tails, the peri-ripple bins, the interval helpers), finding them correct. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; all 32 agree with the record, and for bla-rate-same-across-directions it gave another blocking reason. Points not tied to one claim: the raw voltage reported in 16 files disagrees with the asset metadata (24 other files); the author printed the groups of every file, which confirm the 16 files, and recorded the asset metadata as wrong for ElectricalSeries and ProcessingModule in all 40 files (new finding). M3's rule dropping spikes after the last run epoch is not implemented; the author kept it so and says in the helper docstring why it cannot change any bin used.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the README, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 32 outcomes and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. Points not tied to one claim. The README's run time (10.0 min, six of them streaming) did not match cell 77 (7.2 min) and cell 1 (302 s of loading); the README now gives the final run of this revision (10.2 min, 366 s of loading). The round-1 reasons were found faithful, except that the platform-time point was attributed to habituation-over-days; that entry is corrected.

entries.name: 000061-girardeau-2017
entries.title: Hippocampus and amygdala reactivation during sleep (Girardeau et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the claims of Girardeau, Inema and Buzsaki (2017), written from the full text, the supplement and the paper's code, on dandiset 000061, which holds sorted units of the hippocampus and the amygdala, sleep states, ripple, air puff and reward events from four rats on an air puff linear track task. It tests the unit counts, habituation over days, BLA firing by sleep state, hippocampus-BLA and hippocampus-central nuclei reactivation (explained variance) with all cells, and the ripple rate before and after training. Claims on putative pyramidal cells and on position are blocked, as the dandiset holds neither.
